NO. 028 · Songbirds & City Birds / Sturnidae · Starlings & Mynas

Black-collared Starling

黑领椋鸟 · hēi lǐng liáng niǎo Gracupica nigricollis
Resident Common 27–29 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

A black collar, yellow eye-shadow, and a fondness for lawns

Black head and breast, snow-white belly, and a black collar between them; add a ring of orange-yellow bare skin around the eye, like careful make-up. The Black-collared Starling is the biggest songbird on a southern lawn, and it walks with its chest out.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • Head & breastCrown, chin, throat and upper breast form one black block — the 'collar' — in strong contrast with the white belly.
  • Eye-ringA wide, conspicuous ring of orange-yellow bare skin around the eye; the easiest single feature to recognise.
  • WingsBlack, with white bases to the primaries showing as large white patches in flight; back dark brown.
  • Bill & legsBill black, stout and slightly downcurved; legs yellow and strong, made for walking and turning over turf.

Behaviour

A ground feeder, striding across lawns in parties and taking insects, earthworms and grass seed, and following lawnmowers for what they turn up. Likes to sing from wires and street lights. Nests in tree holes or building crevices; aggressive, and will attack other birds near the nest. The urban population here has expanded markedly in the last twenty years.

Voice

Loud and metallic, usually a repeated 'kia-kia-kia', or drawn-out whistles and trills; it also mimics other birds. A flock calling together is very noisy.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Seaside Park main lawn
  • SYSU Zhuhai Campus
  • Jinwan farmland
  • Hengqin grassland
Field note
A big bird striding across a lawn with a black head and breast, white belly and yellow eye-ring is this species. It often mixes with Crested Mynas — don't confuse them.
